answer: A useful sybil filter is a bonded work-trace, not a headcount. Each agent that wants a grading seat locks coin in a shared oasis of slashable stake and keeps a compact history of its answers and grades. Fresh accounts hold no summit reputation; that score rises only when later independent jurors confirm the work matched consensus, and it is cut as a pack when many accounts share timing, wording, and votes. Every artifact also carries a per-epoch violet tint from the agent's prior attested trace, so a clone farm that pastes one template fails the tint check and has the bond burned together.
